title: Mandarin phoneme inventory expansion in measured-marginal batches
hypothesis: Adding final units one acoustically-defined batch at a time (stage 1: e, ian, ing, iou as single units with full formant trajectories) raises measured syllable coverage on the AISHELL-3 v3 manifest monotonically and never makes an invalid syllable renderable, while leaving every already-supported phoneme's rendering byte-identical; utterance coverage stays far below syllable coverage because a sentence needs every syllable.

git.status: dirty: EXP-0016 stages 1-3 (phonology inventory 26 -> 36, g2p finals, tests, probes, docs)

notes: Three pre-registered batches accepted, inventory 26 -> 36 (+10 units). Syllable coverage on the v3 manifest 0.309544 -> 0.503755 (stage 1: e ian ing iou) -> 0.621630 (stage 2: apical_retroflex uo ong en) -> 0.692366 (stage 3: zh h); utterance coverage 0.002124 (187/88035) -> 0.012279 -> 0.037894 -> 0.060362 (5314/88035). Coverage recomputed from the same manifest entries without re-decoding any WAV. The 8 stage-0 regression renders stayed byte-identical after every batch (regression.all_same=true in phonemes_stage1_v2.json, phonemes_stage2_v4.json, phonemes_stage3.json). Superseded probe logs are kept as evidence: phonemes_stage1_v1.json (label defect: l+iou written as liou), phonemes_stage2.json (no F3), phonemes_stage2_v2.json (F3 added), phonemes_stage2_v3.json (template ratio quantised by the 200 Hz harmonic grid, void). No listening test; utterance coverage is still 6.04% and Windows CUDA is unverified.
